notes.summary: This chapter covers units, motion and the laws of motion, work, energy and power, pressure, light, sound and current electricity at the Class 9-10 NCERT level. RRB Group D in particular sets short numericals (F = ma, kinetic energy, resistors, electricity bills, lens power), while NTPC favours units, instruments and everyday applications.
keyPoints: SI units: force – newton (N), work and energy – joule (J), power – watt (W), pressure – pascal (Pa), frequency – hertz (Hz), current – ampere (A), resistance – ohm (Ω).
Newton's second law: F = m × a. Example: 20 N on 4 kg gives a = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 m/s².
Kinetic energy = ½mv²; potential energy = mgh. Example: 2 kg at 10 m/s has KE = ½ × 2 × 100 = 100 J.
Vertical throw with g = 10 m/s²: maximum height H = u² ÷ 2g, time to top = u ÷ g, total time in air = 2u ÷ g. For u = 20 m/s: H = 20 m, total time = 4 s.
Resistors: series R = R1 + R2 + ...; parallel 1/R = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + .... A parallel combination is always smaller than the smallest single resistor.
R = ρL ÷ A. Stretching a wire to n times its length (volume constant) makes its resistance n² times.
Electrical energy in units = power in kW × hours; 1 unit = 1 kWh. Example: 1000 W for 2 h a day for 30 days = 60 units.
Lens power P = 1 ÷ f (f in metres), unit dioptre (D); convex lens positive, concave lens negative. Myopia is corrected by a concave lens, hypermetropia by a convex lens.
Pascal's law (pressure on an enclosed liquid is transmitted equally in all directions) is the basis of hydraulic lifts, jacks and brakes; Archimedes' principle explains buoyancy.
traps: Forgetting the ½ in kinetic energy, which doubles the answer.
Adding resistances in parallel as if they were in series.
Using focal length in centimetres in P = 1/f: convert to metres first (25 cm = 0.25 m).
For a stretched wire, saying resistance only doubles: the cross-section also halves, so it becomes 4 times.
In vertical-throw questions, giving only the time to reach the top instead of the total time in the air.
notes.examTip: Write the formula, convert every quantity to SI (kg, m, s, and kW for bills), then substitute; most wrong options come from a skipped unit conversion.

questions.text: What is the SI unit of work?
questions.explanation:
Work = force × displacement, so its unit is the newton-metre, which is called the joule (J).
Watt is the unit of power, newton of force and pascal of pressure.
Answer: Joule.

questions.text: A person suffering from myopia (short-sightedness) can see nearby objects clearly but not distant ones. Which lens is used to correct this defect?
questions.explanation:
In myopia the image of a distant object forms in front of the retina, because the eyeball is too long or the eye lens is too strong.
A concave (diverging) lens spreads the rays slightly so that the image moves back onto the retina.
Hypermetropia is corrected with a convex lens and astigmatism with a cylindrical lens.
Answer: Concave lens.

questions.text: What is the SI unit of frequency?
questions.explanation:
Frequency is the number of oscillations per second; 1 hertz (Hz) = 1 oscillation per second.
The decibel measures sound level, the watt measures power and the tesla measures magnetic field strength.
Answer: Hertz.

questions.text: A force of 20 N acts on a body of mass 4 kg kept on a smooth surface. What is the acceleration produced?
questions.explanation:
By Newton's second law, F = m × a, so a = F ÷ m.
a = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 m/s².
(Multiplying gives 80 and dividing the wrong way round gives 0.2, both common slips.)
Answer: 5 m/s².

questions.text: A body of mass 2 kg is moving with a velocity of 10 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
questions.explanation:
Kinetic energy = ½ × m × v².
= ½ × 2 × 10 × 10
= 1 × 100 = 100 J.
(Forgetting the ½ gives 200 J.)
Answer: 100 J.

questions.text: Three resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω and 6 Ω are connected in parallel. What is their equivalent resistance?
questions.explanation:
For resistors in parallel, 1/R = 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6.
Taking LCM 6: 1/R = 3/6 + 2/6 + 1/6 = 6/6 = 1.
So R = 1 Ω, which is less than the smallest resistor (2 Ω), as it must be.
11 Ω would be the series value.
Answer: 1 Ω.

questions.text: An electric heater rated 1000 W is used for 2 hours every day. What is the cost of the electricity it uses in 30 days if one unit costs ₹5?
questions.explanation:
Power = 1000 W = 1 kW.
Energy per day = 1 kW × 2 h = 2 kWh = 2 units.
Energy in 30 days = 2 × 30 = 60 units.
Cost = 60 × ₹5 = ₹300.
Answer: ₹300.

questions.text: What is the power of a convex lens of focal length 25 cm?
questions.explanation:
Power P = 1 ÷ f, where f must be in metres.
f = 25 cm = 0.25 m, so P = 1 ÷ 0.25 = 4 D.
A convex lens has a positive focal length, so P = +4 D.
(Forgetting the reciprocal gives 0.25, and a negative sign would be for a concave lens.)
Answer: +4 D.

questions.text: Hydraulic lifts, hydraulic jacks and hydraulic brakes work on the basis of:
questions.explanation:
Pascal's law states that pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted equally in all directions.
In a hydraulic lift, a small force on a small piston creates a pressure that acts on a large piston, producing a much larger force.
Archimedes' principle explains buoyancy, Bernoulli's principle explains the lift on aircraft wings and Hooke's law relates stress to strain.
Answer: Pascal's law.

questions.text: A metal wire has a resistance of 10 Ω. It is stretched uniformly until its length is doubled, its volume remaining the same. What is its new resistance?
questions.explanation:
R = ρL ÷ A, and volume = L × A stays constant.
If the length becomes 2L, the area must become A ÷ 2.
New R = ρ(2L) ÷ (A/2) = 4 × ρL ÷ A = 4R.
New resistance = 4 × 10 = 40 Ω (20 Ω ignores the change in area).
Answer: 40 Ω.

questions.text: A ball is thrown vertically upward with a velocity of 20 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s² and ignoring air resistance, what are the maximum height reached and the total time the ball stays in the air?
questions.explanation:
At the highest point the velocity becomes 0.
Maximum height: v² = u² – 2gH, so H = u² ÷ 2g = 400 ÷ 20 = 20 m.
Time to reach the top: t = u ÷ g = 20 ÷ 10 = 2 s, and the fall back takes the same 2 s.
Total time in the air = 2 + 2 = 4 s.
Answer: 20 m and 4 s.
